public_rationale: Autonomous ride-hailing provides a counterexample to the categorical present-tense claim under the ordinary reading of exceptionally rapid commercial expansion. The conclusion is narrower than saying this market was profitable or large enough to sustain all of Big Tech. A reading restricted to future growth engines of comparable scale would remain unresolved.
limitations: The result depends on interpreting hypergrowth through commercial adoption rather than a specified revenue threshold.
Company disclosures are not independently audited market totals.
A competitor's exit cautions against treating rapid market expansion as proof of universal business success.
The assessment does not settle the broader prediction about what comes after generative AI.

our_interpretation: Assess the present-tense universal claim that no other technology market was undergoing exceptionally rapid commercial expansion.
Use January through March 2025, the latest completed quarter before publication, for the ongoing observation.
The plain reading permits commercial usage growth as evidence of market expansion; the author does not restrict the claim to revenue or profit.
Autonomous ride-hailing is a distinct commercial market from generative AI products, even though it uses AI.
No arbitrary percentage cutoff or trillion-dollar minimum is imposed. Evidence from multiple suppliers is preferable to one fast-growing company.
criteria.support_condition: Broad evidence shows that plausible technology markets outside generative AI lacked exceptionally rapid commercial expansion during the target period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A credible counterexample shows an existing technology market outside generative AI expanding exceptionally rapidly, supported by commercial operating evidence rather than forecasts alone.
